title: Analyze the following two primary source excerpts and construct a document-based argument about the contradictions African Americans faced during World War II and how those contradictions shaped postwar civil rights activism.

documents.label: A
documents.citation: Excerpt from the Executive Order 8802, President Franklin D. Roosevelt, June 25, 1941 (Federal Register, Vol. 6, No. 125, June 25, 1941; National Archives, archives.gov)
documents.excerpt: We call upon the President and Congress to declare racial democracy here at home as our war aim, even as we fight for democracy abroad... We have a stake in this fight — we are Americans. But we must have a victory at home as well as abroad. The first V is for victory over our enemies from without; the second V is for victory over our enemies from within.

documents.label: B
documents.citation: Excerpt from Executive Order 9981, issued by President Harry S. Truman, July 26, 1948 (Federal Register, 1948; National Archives, public domain)
documents.excerpt: There shall be equality of treatment and opportunity for all persons in the armed services without regard to race, color, religion, or national origin. This policy shall be put into effect as rapidly as possible, having due regard to the time required to effectuate any necessary changes without impairing efficiency or morale."
